See non-blocking finding F-2 for the collapse itself.

evaluate_completion_claim() introduces no new dependency on external reviewer availability; it reuses evaluate(), which already treats external review as optional defense-in-depth, unchanged. The new review-pending rejection in evaluate_completion_claim() (finding F-1) is a stricter, separate completion question, not a merge-authority gate: it never blocks push, candidate admission, governance success, or evaluate()'s own merge-readiness decision, so no reviewer's absence can deadlock merge authority through it.

Each of the six workflows gates execution on the same condition it probes with. hunter-canonicalization-auto.yml's 'Detect trusted canonicalization engine' step tests for exactly the two scripts the job later runs (hunter_collect_learning_observations.py, hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py) and every install, checkout, execute and push step is conditioned on that same output, so the local_git_push step is unreachable whenever the probe reports unavailable, and the unavailable case is surfaced as a named bootstrap message. The two replay workflows probe nothing and admit nothing conditionally: replay-validate runs its entrypoint unconditionally after actions/setup-python, and the privileged replay-publish half is checkout-free and runs only its own inline trusted logic. No in-job self-report stands in as security authority in any of the six.

No candidate-controlled content executes inside a credential-holding boundary. hunter-canonicalization-auto.yml runs only the trusted default-branch copies of its two entrypoints (the first checkout has no path:, so the workspace root is main; the reviewed PR is checked out separately into reviewed-pr/ with persist-credentials: false), and neither hunter_collect_learning_observations.py nor hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py references HUNTER_REGRESSION_ROOT or reads that directory, so the candidate tree is inert data in the job that holds the publication SSH identity. replay-publish holds statuses: write but never checks out, clones, fetches, or executes repository content -- the three trusted files are fetched as inert .fetched text at ref=main and only hashed. replay-validate is the only job that executes candidate controller modules and runs them with GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN explicitly blanked to "" under permissions contents: read.

hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py pushes through the ordinary .githooks/pre-push safety boundary like any human contribution, then opens its Draft PR immediately after push rather than waiting for the hosted Pre-PR Preflight run to complete first -- unlike hunter_issue_agent_candidate_pr.py, which is itself only invoked by a workflow_run trigger after that hosted preflight already passed. This differs because the trust model differs: this script is run by the same identity that authored the content (no elevated-trust PR-opener certifying someone else's unverified candidate), so there is no privileged-attestation-before-proof gap of the kind this family targets. Flagged as a non-blocking design question rather than asserted definitively resolved -- see finding F-5.

scripts/hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py and its test module both import and load cleanly (verified: full mypy run across 865 source files succeeds, and pytest collects and runs both new files without a loader error).

The change widens retryability only where GitHub explicitly reports rate-limit exhaustion: RATE_LIMIT_403_PATTERNS gates the new 403 case in both classify_http_error and classify_cli_failure, so an ordinary permission-denied 403 stays permanent. It adds no budget of any kind -- execute_with_retry still runs exactly policy.attempts iterations with deterministic backoff clamped to policy.max_delay_seconds, no attempt count or deadline is derived from a per-operation timeout, and exhaustion still raises GitHubUnavailable(what, attempts, last) which remains distinguishable from a permanent GitHubRequestError raised on the first non-retryable failure. tests/test_hunter_github_transport.py pins both directions: test_rate_limit_403_is_transient, test_permission_403_remains_permanent, test_cli_rate_limit_403_is_transient.

tests/test_hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py's deterministic assertions run only against repository-owned/local state (a disposable local git remote in tmp_path); the only external-facing calls (`gh`) are stubbed in the test lane, never asserted against a live network response.

No workflow entrypoint gained an undeclared runtime dependency. Both replay entrypoints (hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay.py and hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay_worker.py) import only the standard library, so actions/setup-python alone provisions them and neither job needs a pip step. hunter-canonicalization-auto.yml provisions the engine it installs with 'python -m pip install --only-binary :all: -c requirements/ci-constraints.txt .' before running it, and an engine that is not on the trusted default branch is reported as a named bootstrap condition rather than surfacing as a runtime ImportError. The codeql bridge and governance reconcile changes use only the preinstalled gh CLI and stdlib hashing.

CompletionVerdict is a structured dataclass (accepted: bool, state: str, reason: str) consumers read directly, not prose an agent must parse; `state` is always exactly "COMPLETION_ACCEPTED" or "COMPLETION_REJECTED".

The only change to this file is three additive entries in connector_write_ingress.root_of_trust_paths (hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay.py, hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay_worker.py, hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay_definition.json), which widens declared trust-root coverage rather than relaxing it; no path was removed and no grant was added. The capability is held loudly, not best-effort: hunter_connector_write_ingress.py and hunter_artifact_preflight.py refuse the run when governed trust-root content is unauthorized, and this branch's own pre-push Artifact Guard reported 'PASS: defect registry and changed governed artifacts' over exactly this change. Making the harness a declared trust-root path therefore makes its unauthorized modification fail closed rather than proceed unreported.

The candidate-touching half is pull_request-triggered (never pull_request_target), declares permissions contents: read only, checks out with persist-credentials: false, and blanks GITHUB_TOKEN and GH_TOKEN to "" in both jobs. Candidate controller modules are executed only inside hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay_worker.py, a credential-blanked subprocess; the second job re-checks-out the exact candidate independently and recomputes each scenario's module digest itself via verify_candidate_module_digests() rather than trusting job 1's receipt. The privileged half is workflow_run-triggered (GitHub runs the base repository's own copy), is checkout-free by construction, and independently re-derives trusted_harness_definition_digest, scenario_set_digest, input_fixture_digest and main's tip from read-only API reads at ref=main, comparing the receipt's scenario ids, invariant text, per-scenario outcome, timestamps and overall_result against that trusted definition and treating any missing artifact or field as failure. Publishing a status requires statuses: write in that trusted job, so no candidate test, receipt or self-report can substitute for the independent re-derivation.

The grader is never sourced from the candidate. hunter_trusted_orchestrator_replay.py resolves WORKER_PATH and DEFINITION_PATH from ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] -- the trusted checkout that actions/checkout placed at the default branch -- and loads the scenario set, invariants and fixture from that trusted definition file at import time; _run_scenario() launches that same trusted worker with the candidate supplied only as a confined relative path (resolve_confined_existing refuses any path escaping the workspace root). The privileged publish job independently re-fetches all three grader files at ref=main and refuses a receipt whose trusted_harness_definition_digest, scenario_set_digest or trusted_harness_sha disagrees, so a candidate branch's own copy of the grader can never grade itself. While the grader is not yet on main those ref=main reads fail under 'set -euo pipefail' and the job fails closed; there is no fallback to candidate-supplied grader content.

findings.evidence: AC-5/AC-8 (no false READY / no false completion while review is pending): independent review (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]) confirmed this exact gap on this PR and treated it as P1, which is the signal to stop deferring it. evaluate_completion_claim() now additionally rejects while review_authority reports 'pending' (covers WAITING_FOR_REVIEWER/REVIEW_IN_PROGRESS/POOL_EXHAUSTED), without touching evaluate()'s own merge-readiness decision or its GitHub status output -- so 'currently mergeable' (unaffected, external review remains defense-in-depth per DFF-026) and 'genuinely done' (now stricter) stay correctly distinct.

evaluate_completion_claim() collapses evaluate()'s pending/failure distinction into a single COMPLETION_REJECTED state (DFF-014 evidence above explains why this is safe for this function's specific purpose). A future caller that needs the pending-vs-failure distinction should read CompletionVerdict.reason or call evaluate() directly rather than assume evaluate_completion_claim()'s two-state model is exhaustive.

Real defect found via this session's own adversarial self-review, before hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py was ever proposed: propose() originally rebuilt the dedicated branch unconditionally from main, so a second finding processed while a first finding's PR was still open would silently overwrite the first finding's proposal. Corrected to accumulate on the dedicated branch's own tip unless it is already an ancestor of main.

AC-11's end-to-end proof runs in a controlled local test harness (a disposable local git remote), not against the production fafa33/Project-Hunter registry, because no currently-open, honestly-matching existing defect family was available to demonstrate against without fabricating or misclassifying evidence. This is disclosed explicitly rather than presented as a production demonstration.

hunter_canonicalization_candidate_pr.py opens its Draft PR immediately after push rather than waiting for hosted Pre-PR Preflight to complete first, unlike the trusted-candidate-PR-opener pattern in hunter_issue_agent_candidate_pr.py. See DFF-029 evidence for why the differing trust model makes this a design question rather than a violation; still recorded here for visibility.

Independent review (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], P1) found evaluate_completion_claim() had no production caller -- only the unit tests exercised it, so it could not reject any real worker's completion claim; AC-7/AC-8 were convention, not enforcement. Fixed: hunter_merge_readiness_v2.py gains decide_completion(pr_number), building the same live GitHub observation decide() already uses, and `python scripts/hunter_merge_readiness_v2.py completion <pr>` is now a genuine invokable production path.

Independent review (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], P1) found propose() could silently orphan the dedicated branch forever: if a prior run's push succeeded but its own `gh pr create` call then failed (a transient network blip, a crash), the branch carried real unmerged content with no PR, and every later run computing the identical already-applied observations would just report NO-OP without ever discovering the missing PR. Fixed: propose() now reconciles a real, unmerged, PR-less dedicated branch by opening the missing PR for it, with no new commit needed.
